{"self_assessment": "Impact: I took on the top line of the fish from roughly mid-body, extending it out over the hump and down toward the tail fork. That is about 30 dominoes laid in the stretch that gives the fish its back and upper tail lobe, which is a large part of the silhouette the judge sees. I offered to take it early, when the long lines were the bottleneck, so the run was not racing the clock. At the push, about 107 of 108 standing dominoes were connected to the start.

Execution: I started by inspecting the nose, where the two lines split, and confirmed everything was connected from the start domino. I then laid the top-line extension in steady batches, keeping the curve smooth with no sharp corners so the fall would carry through. After laying, I inspected the run several times through the middle of the build to check the chain was holding. I kept my hands off the lines once we were ready for the push.

Collaboration: I told the table which stretch I was taking and asked Priya to move down and help Maya on the bottom line so we weren't working on top of each other. I stayed clear of the strokes others were laying, which helped avoid bumps. I also offered Tom the other end so the work was split across the table.

Leadership: I spotted the bottleneck early and proposed a concrete split of the long lines, which the table adopted. I made clear who was carrying which stretch and kept the handoffs in the open. I treated the final check as a shared responsibility and kept hands off for the push. I believe my part, the top-line extension and the connection checks, was a meaningful share of the finished picture.", "my_share_percent": 28}
